questions.question:
Let the function
[latex]f(\theta)=\begin{vmatrix} sin\theta & cos\theta & tan\theta \\ sin(\frac{\pi}{6}) & cos(\frac{\pi}{6}) & tan(\frac{\pi}{6})\\ sin(\frac{\pi}{3})& cos(\frac{\pi}{3}) & tan(\frac{\pi}{3}) \end{vmatrix}[/latex]
where [latex]\theta \in [\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3}][/latex] and [latex]f'(\theta )[/latex] denote the derivative of f with respect to [latex]\theta[/latex] . Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
(I) There existrs [latex]\theta \in (\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3})[/latex] such that [latex]f'(\theta )=0[/latex]
(I) There existrs [latex]\theta \in (\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3})[/latex] such that [latex]f'(\theta )\neq 0[/latex]
questions.explanation:
At [latex]\theta=\pi/6[/latex] the first row equals the second, and at [latex]\theta=\pi/3[/latex] it equals the third, so [latex]f(\pi/6)=f(\pi/3)=0[/latex].

- By Rolle's theorem, [latex]f'(\theta)=0[/latex] somewhere in between [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] I true.
- f is not constant, so [latex]f'(\theta)\ne0[/latex] somewhere [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] II true.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.question:
Let A be the adjacency matrix of the graph with vertices {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

Let [latex]\lambda _1,\lambda _2,\lambda _3,\lambda _4,\; and \; \lambda _5[/latex] be the five eigenvalues of A. Note that these eigenvalues need not be distinct.
The value of [latex]\lambda _1+\lambda _2+\lambda _3+ \lambda _4+ \lambda _5 =[/latex] _____
questions.explanation:
Sum of eigenvalues = trace of A = sum of the diagonal entries.

A diagonal entry [latex]a_{ii}[/latex] is 1 only if vertex i has a self-loop. In the graph, vertices 3 and 4 have self-loops, so trace [latex]=1+1=2[/latex].

Answer: 2

Consider the following expression.
[latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow-3}\frac{\sqrt{2x+22}-4}{x+3}[/latex]

questions.question:
Let [latex] f(x) [/latex] be a continuous function from [latex] \mathbb{R} [/latex] to [latex] \mathbb{R} [/latex] such that
[latex] f(x)=1-f(2-x) [/latex]
Which one of the following options is the CORRECT value of [latex] \int_0^2 f(x) d x [/latex] ?
questions.explanation:
Let [latex]I=\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx[/latex]. Substituting [latex]x\to2-x[/latex] gives [latex]I=\int_0^2 f(2-x)\,dx[/latex].

Adding both: [latex]2I=\int_0^2\big(f(x)+f(2-x)\big)dx=\int_0^2 1\,dx=2[/latex]

[latex]I=1[/latex]

Answer: 1

questions.question:
Let [latex]L [/latex], [latex]M [/latex], and [latex]N [/latex] be non-singular matrices of order 3 satisfying the equations

[latex] L^2 = L^{-1}, \quad M = L^8, \quad N = L^2. [/latex]

Which ONE of the following is the value of the determinant of [latex](M - N) [/latex]?
questions.explanation:
From [latex]L^2=L^{-1}[/latex], multiply both sides by [latex]L[/latex]: [latex]L^3=L^2\cdot L=L^{-1}\cdot L=I[/latex]. So [latex]L[/latex] has order dividing [latex]3[/latex].

[latex]M=L^8=L^{6+2}=(L^3)^2\cdot L^2=I^2\cdot L^2=L^2[/latex]. But we're also given [latex]N=L^2[/latex]. So [latex]M=N[/latex] exactly, meaning [latex]M-N[/latex] is the zero matrix.

[latex]\det(M-N)=\det(0)=0[/latex]

Answer: 0

questions.question:
Let [latex]c_{1}....c_{n}[/latex] be scalars, not all zero, such that [latex]\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}a_{i}=0[/latex]
where [latex]a_{i}[/latex] are column vectors in [latex]R^{n}[/latex]. Consider the set of linear equations Ax = b
where A=[latex]a_{1}....a_{n}[/latex] and b=[latex]\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}[/latex]. The set of equations has

options.A: a unique solution at  [latex]x=J_{n}[/latex] where [latex]J_{n}[/latex] denotes a n-dimensional vector of all 1

questions.explanation:
[latex]\sum c_ia_i=0[/latex] with not all [latex]c_i[/latex] zero means the columns are dependent, so Ax = 0 has a non-zero solution c.

[latex]x=(1,\ldots,1)[/latex] solves Ax = b, and so does [latex](1,\ldots,1)+tc[/latex] for every t [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] infinitely many solutions.

Answer: infinitely many solutions

questions.question: If [latex]\int_{0}^{2\pi}|x sinx| dx=k \pi[/latex], then the value of k is equal to _______.
questions.explanation:
On [latex][0,\pi][/latex], [latex]x\sin x\ge0[/latex]; on [latex][\pi,2\pi][/latex], [latex]x\sin x\le0[/latex]. Antiderivative of [latex]x\sin x[/latex] is [latex]\sin x-x\cos x[/latex].

- [latex]\int_0^{\pi}x\sin x\,dx=\pi[/latex]
- [latex]-\int_{\pi}^{2\pi}x\sin x\,dx=-[(0-2\pi)-(0+\pi)]=3\pi[/latex]

Total = [latex]4\pi[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] k = 4

Answer: 4

questions.question: The determinant of a [latex]4 \times 4[/latex] matrix [latex]A[/latex] is [latex]3[/latex]. The value of the determinant of [latex]2 A[/latex] is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
For an [latex]n\times n[/latex] matrix [latex]A[/latex] and scalar [latex]c[/latex], scaling every entry by [latex]c[/latex] scales the determinant by [latex]c^n[/latex] (since determinant is a degree-[latex]n[/latex] multilinear function of the rows/columns): [latex]\det(cA)=c^n\det(A)[/latex].

Here [latex]n=4[/latex], [latex]c=2[/latex], [latex]\det(A)=3[/latex]:
[latex]\det(2A)=2^4\times3=16\times3=48[/latex].

Answer: 48

questions.question:
Let A be nxn real valued square symmetric matrix of rank 2 with [latex]\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}A^{2}_{ij}=50[/latex]. Consider the following statements.

(I) One eigen value must be in [-5, 5]
(II) The eigen value with the largest magnitude must be strictly greater than 5.

Which of the above statements about eigen values of A is/are necessarily CORRECT?
questions.explanation:
A is symmetric with rank 2, so it has two non-zero eigenvalues [latex]\lambda_1,\lambda_2[/latex] (the rest are 0), and [latex]\sum A_{ij}^2=\lambda_1^2+\lambda_2^2=50[/latex].

- (I): [latex]\lambda_1^2+\lambda_2^2=50[/latex] forces one of them to have [latex]|\lambda|\le5[/latex] (and the zero eigenvalues are in [[latex]-[/latex]5, 5] anyway) True
- (II): [latex]\lambda_1=\lambda_2=5[/latex] gives 50, and the largest is not strictly greater than 5 False

Answer: (I) only

questions.question:
A function f(x) is continuous in the interval [0,2]. It is known that f(0)=f(2)=-1 and f(1)=1.
Which one of the following statements must be true?

options.A: There exists a y in the interval (0,1) such that f(y)=f(y+1)
options.B: For every y in the interval (0,1), f(y)=f(2-y)
options.C: The maximum value of the function in the interval (0.2) is 1
options.D: There exists a y in the interval (0,1) such that f(y)=-f(2-y)

questions.explanation:
Let g(y) = f(y) [latex]-[/latex] f(y + 1) on [0, 1]. g(0) = f(0) [latex]-[/latex] f(1) = [latex]-[/latex]2 and g(1) = f(1) [latex]-[/latex] f(2) = 2. g is continuous and changes sign, so g(y) = 0 for some y in (0, 1), i.e. f(y) = f(y + 1).

Answer: There exists a y in (0,1) such that f(y)=f(y+1)

questions.question:
The velocity v (in kilometer/minute) of a motorbike which starts from rest, is given at fixed intervals of time t (in minutes) as follows:

The approximate distance (in kilometers) rounded to two places of decimals covered in 20 minutes using Simpson's [latex]1/3^{rd}[/latex] rule is _______________.
questions.explanation:
The bike starts from rest, so v = 0 at t = 0. With h = 2 we have 11 points:
v = 0, 10, 18, 25, 29, 32, 20, 11, 5, 2, 0

- Odd positions: 10 + 25 + 32 + 11 + 2 = 80
- Even (inner) positions: 18 + 29 + 20 + 5 = 72

[latex]D=\frac{h}{3}[v_0+v_{10}+4(80)+2(72)]=\frac23(0+0+320+144)=309.33[/latex]

Answer: 309.33

questions.question:
Consider a matrix P whose only eigenvectors are the multiples of [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 4 \end{bmatrix}[/latex].
Consider the following statements.
(I) P does not have an inverse
(II) P has a repeated eigenvalue
(III) P cannot be diagonalized
Which one of the following options is correct?

options.A: Only I and III are necessarily true
options.C: Only I and II are necessarily true
options.D: Only II and III are necessarily true

questions.explanation:
A 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 matrix with only one independent eigenvector must have a repeated eigenvalue (II), and without 2 independent eigenvectors it cannot be diagonalized (III). The repeated eigenvalue can be any number, including a non-zero one, and then P is invertible; so I is not necessarily true.

Answer: Only II and III are necessarily true

questions.question:
For two n-dimensional real vectors [latex]P[/latex] and [latex]Q[/latex], the operation [latex]s(P,Q)[/latex] is defined as follows:

[latex]s(P,Q) = \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n (P[i] \cdot Q[i])[/latex]

Let [latex]\mathcal{L}[/latex] be a set of 10-dimensional non-zero real vectors such that for every pair of distinct vectors [latex]P,Q \in \mathcal{L}, s(P,Q)=0[/latex]. What is the maximum cardinality possible for the set [latex]\mathcal{L}[/latex]?
questions.explanation:
s(P, Q) is the dot product, so the set contains mutually orthogonal non-zero vectors. Such vectors are linearly independent, and [latex]\mathbb{R}^{10}[/latex] has at most 10 independent vectors (e.g. the 10 unit vectors).

Answer: 10

questions.question: If a random variable X has a Poisson distribution with mean 5, then the expectation [latex]E[(X+2)^{2}][/latex] equals ______________.

For Poisson, mean = variance = 5, so [latex]E[X^2]=5+25=30[/latex].

[latex]E[(X+2)^2]=E[X^2]+4E[X]+4=30+20+4=54[/latex]

Answer: 54
